issues.issue: The Term ends on the tenth anniversary of the Commencement Date, but Section 8.4.1 provides that the Term is not deemed to expire until services transfer assistance is complete, and Section 8.4.3 allows a further year's extension.
Section 2.54 defines a 'Renewal Decision' as a decision 'conforming to the requirements of Section 3.2', but this Section imposes no decision requirements at all.

The window 'from thirty (30) to thirty-two (32) months prior to expiration' is stated as a period running backwards, and combined with 'time being of the essence' the consequence of a late request is not stated.
Section 3.6.1.3(d) contemplates the consequences of neither Party issuing a Request for Renewal, so the failure to request has price consequences this Section does not mention.
Negotiations may be terminated 'at any time after the date that is twenty-eight (28) months prior to expiration', which leaves the earlier two-month period locked in without saying so expressly.
'five (5) anniversaries after the commencement of the last agreed Renewal Term' is an unusual formulation for a five-year period.
The rights arise 'upon expiration of the Term' subject to cure of 'any existing defaults', without saying who determines whether a default exists or how a disputed default affects the right.

The heading of Section 3.6 promises rights 'Upon Termination or Expiration' and Section 3.6.1.8 dates the lease from 'termination or expiration', yet this operative text confers rights only on expiration.
'between four (4) and eight (8) strands' with a maximum capped at ten percent of strands 'in any given portion' does not say who selects the number or how 'portion' is measured.
The exclusion is keyed to strand counts 'as of the Termination Date', a term used nowhere else and inconsistent with Section 3.6.1, which grants the right only on expiration of the Term.
The measurement period runs to 'the last calendar quarter before the date of the Request for Renewal', which is undefined and may never occur if no request is made.
Section 3.6.1.3(d) expressly contemplates that neither Party issues a Request for Renewal, in which case this Section's measurement date does not exist.
The table's discount is computed on 'invested' amounts that include an accumulated net operating loss under 3.6.1.2(b), so 'investment' is defined to include losses as well as expenditures.
Section 3.6.1.7 caps total discounts at $6,000,000 while this table can generate larger discounts on investments well above $10,000,000, so the two must be reconciled.
The table begins at 'At least $3,000,000' and supplies no price where the Operator has invested less than that amount.
Section 3.6.2 removes the rights entirely where the Operator declines renewal and has invested less than $3,000,000, so the gap in this table is filled only by reading the two together.
The provision cross-refers to 'Section 3.6.1.3 or 3.1.6.4', a transposed citation that does not exist, and to 'the same methodology as in Section 4.9.4' when the methodology is in Section 4.9.4.2.
Section 3.6.1.10 uses 'the CPI as in Section 4.9.4.2' for the same adjustment mechanism, showing the citation here is astray.
Pricing on 'the highest number of strands leased in any Network Segment' does not say whether that number is multiplied across the whole network or applied once.
Section 3.6.1.11 makes disclaimed strands void and excludes disclaimed mileage from cost shares, which pulls against pricing the exercise 'regardless of disclaimers of use'.

Payment is due 'on or before the end of the Term', yet Section 3.6.1 makes the right arise only upon expiration of the Term and Section 8.4.1 says the Term is not deemed to end until transfer assistance is complete.
The $6,000,000 cap cannot be squared with the tables in Sections 3.6.1.3 and 3.6.1.4, which generate dollar-for-dollar discounts without limit above $10,000,000 of investment.

The lease commences 'upon termination or expiration of the Term', although Section 3.6.1 makes the underlying right arise only on expiration and Section 3.6.2 denies it where MTC terminates for cause.
'MTC's policies then applicable to others' and 'then-prevailing prices' leave the Operator's post-term costs to be set unilaterally later.

'half the actual maintenance costs ... during the last two full calendar year prior to the exercise' is ungrammatical and does not say whether the baseline is half of one year or half of the two-year total.

The stated formula divides maintenance costs by total fiber miles and multiplies by a strand ratio and actual mileage, which does not reproduce 'a pro rata share ... based on the percentage of strands' as the same Section describes it.
Section 3.6.1.5(b) prices the exercise 'regardless of disclaimers of use made pursuant to Section 3.6.1.11', which is difficult to reconcile with disclaimed rights being wholly void here.

The trailing condition 'and the Network Operator has invested less than $3,000,000' is placed so that it may qualify only limb (b) or both limbs, and 'In either such event' then refers back to two limbs of uncertain content.

Section 3.6.1.4 assumes an Operator-initiated non-renewal still yields dark fiber rights priced from $3,000,000 upward, which is hard to square with this Section's forfeiture in the same circumstances.

'responsible for all aspects of the management, sales, monitoring, operations, support, and maintenance' followed by responsibilities that 'include, generally' leaves the enumerated list's relationship to the general grant unresolved.

'Attachment Database' and 'Fiber Management Plan' obligations are imposed here from the Effective Date, but Section 4.3.4 makes the Operator responsible for the Attachment Database only from the Commencement Date.
'Initial Plan' is capitalised here but Section 4.9.3.1 refers only to 'an initial plan', and no definition of the term appears in Article 2.
Section 4.5.2 requires the Fiber Management Plan draft within six months 'after execution of this Agreement' while 4.1.10.4 measures the same six months from the Effective Date.
'shall be reasonably adjusted' fixes no mechanism, no adjuster and no measure of the adjustment.

MTC's sole responsibility for design and construction sits against Section 4.9.2.9, in which MTC only agrees to take 'commercially reasonable steps' toward a design facilitating the Operator's performance.
'promptly after the Effective Date' and 'in such detail as MTC may reasonably request' set no measurable standard for the marketing obligation.

Deemed acceptance runs from 'receipt of such results', but MTC is only obliged to give notice of testing 'when doing so will not adversely impact the construction schedule', so the Operator may be deemed to accept tests it never learned of.

The direction that Article 11's time periods 'shall be reduced by eighty percent (80%)' cannot be applied coherently to Article 11's structure, which fixes a fifteen, thirty and forty-five day escalation ladder and arbitrator-selection windows.

The Operator must perform additional services if MTC 'requires' them while the Parties merely 'shall negotiate an amendment ... that affords commercially reasonable terms', an agreement to agree on price after performance.
'all information, material, documentation, and reports that may be reasonably required or requested by MTC' is an open-ended assistance obligation followed by illustrative specifics.
The Ramp-Up Plan requires 'approval by MTC, EOPSS and ITD', two of whom are not parties, and the contents 'need not be limited to' the listed items.

Section 4.1.10.6 requires the Ramp-Up Plan draft 'within 9 months of the Effective Date' while this Section requires submission within nine months of a start date thirty days after the Effective Date.
'The Parties intend that ...' states purpose rather than obligation, and 'reasonable accommodation' is not defined.
The intention that ITD and EOPSS bear activities outside the demarcation point depends on the demarcation definition that Section 4.5.2.4 leaves to be settled later in the Fiber Management Plan.

Responsibility commences on segment acceptance, whereas Section 4.9.1 makes the Operator pay all operating costs from the Effective Date and Section 4.9.6 keys the CAPEX payments to the Commencement Date.
'the Contract Price' is capitalised but nowhere defined, and the sentence ends with a stray double period.
Article 2 states that all capitalised terms take their meaning from that Article, yet 'Contract Price' and the Design-Build Contractor's agreement terms are not defined there.
The 'Attachment Database' is defined only by reference to a separate agreement with a third-party project manager to which the Operator is not a party.
Section 4.1.2 already obliges the Operator to maintain records in the Attachment Database as a general Article 4 responsibility, while this Section starts that duty only at the Commencement Date.
'the then-current version of Exhibit G' contemplates that the exhibit may change, without saying who may change it or how.
Section 12.1 permits modification of the Agreement only by a signed writing, which is hard to square with an exhibit having a shifting 'then-current version'.
'mutually and regularly consult' imposes no measurable frequency or consequence.

The six-month clock here runs from 'execution of this Agreement' while Section 4.1.10.4 runs the same deadline from the Effective Date, and Section 2.15 defines the Effective Date by a blank in the preamble.
The Section states only when MTC 'will not approve' the plan and never says MTC must approve one that satisfies the listed criteria, and 'excessive stranded segments' has no measure.
Section 12.13.1 requires consents not to be unreasonably withheld, which pulls against a provision framed entirely as grounds for refusal.
'Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Section' is ambiguous as to whether 'this Section' means 4.5.4 alone or the whole of Section 4.5, which determines whether 4.5.5 is carved out.
Section 4.5.5 makes Network Operator Network Extensions 'the sole property of the Network Operator', which the narrower reading of this exception would contradict.
'to expand beyond the MTC Network' does not say how an extension that is physically attached to and served by the MTC Network is distinguished from part of it.

Section 2.39 makes any fiber extension part of the MTC Network unless the Operator proves otherwise, which cannot be squared with an extension being 'the sole property of the Network Operator' by default here.
'qualified contractors' sets no standard and the Section does not say who pays for the Interconnection work.
Customer-funded extensions are the customer's sole property, yet Section 2.39 provides that a fiber extension becomes part of the MTC Network unless the Network Operator establishes otherwise.
'the same role and rights relative to the MBI Network Extensions as are set forth in section 4.2' imports an advisory role written for the initial construction into a different context.

MTC owns any MBI Network Extension 'regardless of the source of its funding', which cannot be squared with Section 2.36's definition requiring MTC funding in whole or in part, nor with Section 4.5.6.3's customer ownership.
'carrier-grade quality and reliability' fixes no measurable upgrade obligation, and the Section both requires periodic upgrades and caps them at available fund balances.

The upgrade duty is funded only from the CAPEX Fund under Section 4.9.6, but Section 4.9.1 makes the Operator pay 'all ongoing costs of operating the MTC Network', leaving the boundary between the two contested.
Tasks 'whether or not specifically described in this Agreement' are deemed included if 'required for the proper performance and provision of the Services', an open-ended sweep-in with no boundary.
This implied-scope rule pulls against Section 12.1, which makes the written Agreement the entire agreement and permits change only by signed writing.
The Section caps rates by reference both to 'Price Caps in Exhibit F' and, for state agencies, to '85% of the applicable rates in the then-current Price Schedule', two different benchmarks.
The Agreement's exhibit list places the Price Caps in Exhibit D and assigns Exhibit F to the Master Services Agreement with EOPSS and ITD, so the cross-reference here points to the wrong exhibit.

The present assignment of all Third Party Service Provider contracts to MTC on termination sits against Section 12.10, which bars assignment of the Agreement without consent and requires assignees expressly to assume obligations.

The Operator acts as MTC's agent for dark fiber leases, yet Section 4.7.4.5 gives it 50% of the payments and Section 2.45 treats that share as its own Network Revenue, which is difficult to square with a pure agency.

'at a the price of $60/mile/strand/month' is ungrammatical, and 'as the same may be adjusted from time to time in accordance with this Agreement' leaves it unclear whether the fixed figure or the Price Schedule governs.
The reference to 'the Pricing Schedule' does not match the defined term 'Price Schedule' in Section 2.53, and a fixed $60 rate sits against the Price Caps regime in Sections 2.52 and 4.7.5.
A compliant lease still requires MTC approval here, which sits against Section 4.7.4.1's premise that standard terms have already been 'approved in advance by MTC'.
'with the expectation that' federal national-security leases 'will be accommodated' and that 'favorable consideration will be given' creates obligations of uncertain force.

The Operator leases extension fiber 'in its own name' and keeps the revenue, while Section 2.45 excludes such revenue and Section 4.7.4.5 splits only MTC Network dark fiber payments, so contiguous circuits may fall on either side.

The 50/50 split of IRU payments must be read together with Section 2.45, which both includes the Operator's share in Network Revenue and excludes MTC's share, so lump-sum IRU payments are shared but then re-shared under Section 4.9.5.

The Price Caps are said to be 'set forth in Exhibit F' although the Agreement's exhibit list assigns Price Caps to Exhibit D, and the amendment route 'pursuant to ARTICLE 6' conflicts with Section 6.2's requirement of written approval of both Parties.
Publication of the Price Schedule sits against Section 2.9(b), which treats fee structures as Confidential Information.
'To the extent requested by the Network Operator' makes the annual update optional, while the following sentence assumes increases will occur and conditions only above-CPI increases on approval.

Allowing Price Caps to be updated annually on the Operator's request conflicts with Section 4.7.5, which makes Exhibit F amendable only pursuant to Article 6, and with Section 6.2's requirement of written approval of both Parties.

The prohibition 'Network Operator shall not provide Retail Services' is self-defeating because Section 2.57 defines Retail Service as services provided by a Third Party Service Provider, which Section 2.64 defines to exclude the Network Operator.

MTC's audit right over an Affiliate's 'Retail Service activities' reaches a non-party, which sits against Section 12.11's bar on conferring rights on non-parties and against Section 12.10's assignment limits.

'all other operating and monitoring expenses contemplated by this Agreement' is a general catch-all closing a long enumerated list, and its reach against the enumerated exclusions that follow is contestable.

The Operator pays 'all ongoing costs of operating the MTC Network' while Section 4.6.1 funds updates and upgrades from the CAPEX Fund held by MTC, leaving the boundary between operating cost and capital upgrade unresolved.
Agreements are provided 'for informational purposes only', yet Section 4.9.2.4 makes previously disclosed terms the benchmark for identifying materially different terms.
'the responsibilities described in this Agreement' with respect to unidentified draft agreements does not specify what those responsibilities are.

'other purposes aimed at maintaining or enhancing the extent, structure, functioning and viability of the MTC Network, including but not limited to' is an open-ended catch-all that expands the Operator's future obligations without limit.
The estimate must compare the proposed term 'with the most expensive alternative contractual term recommended by Network Operator', a comparator that perversely minimises the measured increment.
The Section makes the estimate 'a precondition to exercising the right to object set forth in Section 4.9.2.5', but Section 4.9.2.5 confers a credit and creates no right to object.

The credit is for costs incurred 'as a result of MTC's agreeing to the contractual term objected to', although the Section itself provides no objection procedure and 'shall be entitled take a credit' omits a word.
Section 4.9.2.4 conditions a 'right to object' on the cost estimate, but no such right is created here or anywhere else in the Agreement.

The Operator is MTC's agent but has no authority to modify third-party agreements, which sits against Sections 4.1.8 and 4.1.9 making it 'administratively responsible for ensuring compliance' with those agreements.

Reduction 'in proportion to the average shortfall (from 90%) in the percentage of CAIs that have been connected as of the end of each week' is a formula whose application to a payment amount is not stated.
The reduction applies to payments under Section 4.9.6, but those CAPEX payments begin only after the Commencement Date, so there are no such payments in the window this Section addresses.
'MTC represents and agrees that it will seek advice ... and take commercially reasonable steps' blends a representation with a future covenant of uncertain content.
Section 4.2.1 makes MTC 'solely responsible' for design decisions, which sits against this promise that the network will be designed to facilitate the Operator's achievement of its parameters.

Section 4.1.10.1 calls the same document the 'Initial Plan' as a capitalised term, while this Section refers only to 'an initial plan' and Section 2.4 defines the separate 'Annual Plan' by reference to Section 4.9.2.
'Beginning with the first business day of the fourth quarter ... and by the beginning of each fourth calendar quarter thereafter' is an awkward formulation of an annual deadline.
Section 2.4 defines the Annual Plan as the plan submitted 'pursuant to Section 4.9.2', not this Section, so the defined term points elsewhere.
'paid annually in four (4) equal parts at the beginning of each calendar quarter, commencing with the Effective Date' does not say whether 'Year 1' runs from the Effective Date or by calendar year.
The footnote escalates by 'the CPI' for years beyond Year 10, while Section 4.9.4.2 supplies a different multiplier expressed as 100 plus the CPI increase.

'100 plus the increase in CPI ... stated as a percentage' is ambiguous between the index-point rise and the percentage rise, and the worked example (150 to 165 giving 110%) shows the text does not say what it means.
The same methodology is imported by Sections 3.6.1.5(a), 3.6.1.10 and 4.7.5.2, so the ambiguity propagates into dark-fibre pricing and price-schedule increases.
'CPI Escalation' is capitalised and used as though defined, but no such term appears in Article 2 or elsewhere.

The three tiers are joined by 'plus', which supports a marginal-rate reading, but each is phrased as a percentage 'on annual Network Revenue greater than' a threshold, which supports a whole-amount reading.
Payment is due within 45 days after the Operator's fiscal year, while Section 4.9.8 states that any payment to MTC 'shall be paid quarterly unless another payment schedule is specified herein'.
